name: Nu Holdings
thesis: Latin America's leading digital bank (Brazil + Mexico + Colombia). In Brazil — now a mature, ~60%+ penetrated market — the story shifts from customer adds to monetization: ARPAC compounding as cohorts deepen product penetration into credit card, personal loan, investments, and insurance, with risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk) expanding as cost-to-serve stays near-zero. In Mexico and Colombia, total customer count remains the primary signal — these are the new acquisition engines, compounding on network effects and low CAC, but Mexico's credit book mix is the watch-item (unhedged expansion if it grows >50% QoQ). Bet: durable Brazil profitability — ROE crossing 30% on a consolidated basis, held above a 25% floor — funds growth-market expansion while consolidated revenue growth holds the 25%+ track and CET1 stays above 13%. Thesis breaks if ROE sustains below 25% for two quarters, risk-adjusted NIM contracts YoY for two quarters, revenue growth decelerates by more than 80% versus the prior-year same quarter, consolidated NPL 15d+ deteriorates YoY by more than 150bps for two same-fiscal-quarter prints, or net customer adds fall below 5M/Q while Brazil flagship-product penetration rolls over QoQ. Monetization is already inflecting, not pending: monthly ARPAC is ~$16 and compounding while risk-adjusted NIM expands and the credit book has seasoned well through Brazil's high-Selic period (90d+ NPL eased from the ~7.0% Q3'24 peak to ~6.5%, with the Q1'26 early-stage uptick seasonal). Bull-case optionality: the U.S. (Nubank, N.A. — OCC charter approved Jan-2026, ~mid/late-2027 launch) is a deliberate, bounded 'call option' framed by management at <100bps consolidated-efficiency drag and contingent on product-market fit, wedging into the Latin-American diaspora via Spanish-language banking and remittances; Mexico (banking license Apr-2025, Q1'26 break-even) and Colombia (3rd-largest market, ~5M customers) compound the multi-country engine. Valuation is the entry edge — PEG ~0.5 and the cheapest forward multiple since the 2021 IPO — but downside is NOT structurally capped: high beta (~1.45), ~70% of revenue in Brazil, and the NU+MELI pair concentrate a single leveraged bet on the Brazilian consumer and the real (Selic still restrictive at ~14.5%), so the residual risk is macro/FX/concentration, not a capped drawdown.
key_driver: Customer count × ARPAC × NIM with NPL controlled
chart_priorities: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
Capital adequacy ratio (CET1 / Basel III total)
Credit exposure by product x country

tier_1_kpis.name: ROE (annualized, consolidated)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Consolidated ROE <25% for 2 consecutive Qs (thesis bet is ROE crossing 30% durably)

tier_1_kpis.name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Risk-adjusted NIM contracts YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (cost of risk outrunning NIM expansion)

tier_1_kpis.name: Capital adequacy ratio (CET1 / Basel III total)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Capital ratio falls below 13% OR drops >150bps QoQ without explicit growth-deployment rationale (cushion erosion)

tier_1_kpis.name: NPL 15d+ ratio (consolidated total: early-stage 15-90d + severe 90d+, YoY-tracked)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Total NPL (15d+ consolidated) YoY deterioration >150bps for 2 consecutive Qs in the same fiscal quarter — YoY framing controls for LatAm consumer-credit seasonality; absolute level is allowed to drift with the evolving underwriting mix, but rapid YoY worsening signals a credit-cycle break rather than a seasonal pattern

tier_1_kpis.name: Monthly ARPAC (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: ARPAC growth <15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: Product penetration by country (% of customers using each product, Brazil/Mexico/Colombia x credit card/personal loan/investments/insurance)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Brazil flagship-product penetration declines QoQ for 2 consecutive Qs OR Mexico penetration ramp stalls

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit exposure by product x country (loan book mix: credit card / personal loan / SMB / FGTS, split Brazil/Mexico/Colombia)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Single-product concentration >60% of consolidated book OR Mexico credit book grows >50% QoQ (unhedged expansion risk)

tier_1_kpis.name: Total customers (millions)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Net adds <5M per quarter for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_2_kpis.name: NPL 90d+ by product (credit card vs personal loan vs SMB) — early warning on which product cycle is breaking

thesis_breakers_qualitative: ROE fails to durably cross 30% / drifts below 25% (exceptional-profitability thesis breaks)
Risk-adjusted NIM stops expanding (pricing power vs. credit-cost balance lost)
Capital cushion erodes without growth-deployment rationale

Total NPL (15d+ consolidated) deteriorates YoY beyond ~150bps in the same fiscal quarter — i.e. worsening that exceeds seasonality and is not explained by deliberate underwriting-mix shifts (credit-cycle break)

Concentration / correlated macro: NU + MELI are a doubled-up bet on the Brazilian consumer and the BRL (Selic ~14.5%); a Brazil credit-cycle or real drawdown hits both holdings at once — downside is correlated, not capped.
U.S. call-option fails its bounds: efficiency drag exceeds the <100bps cap, or no credible product-market fit (Spanish/remittance) appears by ~2027 — optionality turns into ongoing cost.

break_rules.kpi_name: Revenue YoY Growth Deceleration (YoY of YoY growth rate)
break_rules.narrative: Revenue YoY growth rate decelerates by more than 80% compared to the same quarter a year prior (e.g. prior-year same-Q YoY growth of 30% collapsing to <6% this Q). Thesis bet is consolidated revenue growth holding 25%+; a single-quarter 80%+ collapse in the growth rate itself signals the growth engine has stalled, even if absolute revenue is still nominally positive YoY.
Consolidated ROE below 25% for 2 consecutive quarters — thesis bet is durable ROE crossing 30%; sustained sub-25% means the exceptional-profitability story is broken.
Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk) contracting YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — either pricing power is eroding or cost of risk is outrunning yield, undermining the expanding-spread thesis.
Capital ratio below 13% — prudent-cushion thesis breaks; well-capitalized banks in LatAm typically run 14-18%, sub-13% signals either aggressive deployment or stress.

Consolidated NPL (15d+ total, covering both early-stage 15-90d and severe 90d+) deteriorating YoY by more than 150bps (1.5pp) for 2 consecutive quarters in the same fiscal quarter comparison. YoY framing rather than absolute level — the underwriting mix legitimately shifts the steady-state NPL ratio (more credit card / SMB / FGTS each have different baseline NPLs), so absolute thresholds break as the book evolves. YoY same-quarter comparison neutralizes LatAm consumer-credit ...

business_model_rules.narrative: 90d+ NPL > 7% for 2Q — credit-quality break; their underwriting thesis depends on the 5-6% historical range holding.
Monthly ARPAC < $10 for 2Q — cross-sell stalling; expanding ARPAC is the unit-economics flywheel.
Activity rate < 82% for 2Q — customers becoming dormant; engagement-flywheel signal.
15-90d NPL > 5% for 2Q — leading indicator of cohort credit deterioration; fires 1-2Q before 90d+ trips.

bull_case_legs: Re-rating from a historically low multiple: PEG ~0.5, ~15x forward — cheapest since the Dec-2021 IPO. Base case ~10%+ IRR (double in ~7yr) without re-rating; 15-20% IRR (double in ~4-5yr) with re-rating. Note: a literal 3yr double needs ~26% CAGR, just above the 20% bull top-end.

U.S. optionality (Nubank, N.A.): OCC charter approved 2026-01-29; fund-by ~Jan-2027, operate-by ~mid/late-2027; bounded <100bps efficiency drag, PMF-contingent; diaspora wedge = Spanish-language banking + remittances. A near-free option, not yet a paid-for growth leg.
Multi-country compounding: Mexico (banking license Apr-2025, Q1'26 break-even) + Colombia (3rd market, ~5M customers) extend the low-CAC acquisition engine beyond a maturing Brazil.
Monetization inflection: ARPAC ~$16/mo and rising, risk-adjusted NIM ~9.5% and expanding YoY, on a credit book that seasoned through high-Selic Brazil (90d+ NPL ~6.5%, off the ~7.0% Q3'24 peak).
